readonly_folder_check.verified_against_pool: Exact match: id 1971631 -> TC-54455, id 1971632 -> TC-54456, both test_case_folder_id 764093. info.count (2) == len(test_cases) (2).

scratch_folder_flag_comparison.note: Exercised the pool's __scratch__ folder (764138) both with and without include_subfolders_tc, specifically to check for the list_test_plans_v1-style count/rows desync when a subfolder flag inflates the array. Result: NOT PRESENT here -- info.count tracked len(test_cases) correctly in both branches.

branch_include_subfolders_tc_true.count_vs_rows: info.count (19) == len(test_cases) (19) -- matches. The extra row (TC-54458, id 1975349) carries test_case_folder_id 764828, the direct child of 764138 -- consistent with the pool's documented 18-direct/19-total split.

folders_block.actual: object keyed by (stringified) folder id -> array of ancestor-chain entries, each {id: integer, name: string, parent_id: integer|null, ui_position: integer}. Observed keys '764138' (the invoked folder itself, one entry, parent_id null) and '764828' (the child that holds the extra case, two entries: itself with parent_id 764138, then 764138 again as the root of that chain).
folders_block.finding: This is a real instance of the 'unfalsifiable {type:object}' pattern -- the contract promises nothing checkable about `folders`, and the actual shape (a folder-id-keyed map of ancestor chains) is a genuine, non-trivial structure worth declaring.

declared_missing: test_cases[].test_case_steps -- declared as a nested object (background, feature, scenario, hashed_id, id, order, project_id, result, sharedStep, shared_step_detail_id, shared_step_id, step, test_data, test_case_id, test_recording_id, title, created_at, updated_at); every observed row across both folders (20 rows total) returns an empty ARRAY instead. This is a type mismatch, not just an empty-collection ambiguity -- the container type itself disagrees with the contract, so none of those nested fields are reachable via this response shape.
undeclared_returned: test_cases[].automation_state -- a full descriptor object (id, internal_name, field_name, colour, value_category, name), entirely absent from the declared schema, which documents only the differently-shaped automation_status:{name,value}. The two co-exist on every row and describe the same underlying state.
test_cases[].priority.value_category -- undeclared extra key on the otherwise-matching priority object (always null in observations)

folders (top-level, only present when include_subfolders_tc=true) -- declared as bare {type:object}; see scratch_folder_flag_comparison.branch_include_subfolders_tc_true.folders_block for the actual shape

notes: Both pool folders exercised as instructed. __readonly__ (764093) round-tripped exactly: 2 rows, ids/identifiers matching the pool record verbatim, info.count == len(rows). __scratch__ (764138) exercised both with and without include_subfolders_tc: 18 rows direct (info.count 18), 19 rows with the flag (info.count 19, extra row correctly attributed to child folder 764828). COUNT-VS-ROWS was checked deliberately per the standing caution about list_test_plans_v1's flag-triggered desync (15/29 rows vs a stuck count of 15) -- that defect does NOT reproduce here; this capability's info.count stayed in sync with len(test_cases) in every branch. Container/folder-id consistency also checked: test_case_folder_id on each row matches the folder its `links.folder` points at, including the subfolder row surfaced only by the recursive flag -- no container mismatch found. status and case_type were null on every one of the 20 rows observed (no case in either pool folder has a custom status or case_type set), so their declared nested shapes (id/internal_name/field_name/colour/name) could not be positively verified against a non-null value -- flagged as an unverified sub-shape rather than folded into the DRIFT verdict, since it doesn't contradict the contract, just leaves it unexercised. Verdict is DRIFT rather than PASS on the strength of two things: the test_case_steps object-vs-array type mismatch (declared_missing, shallowest path picked per instruction) and a substantial undeclared-field list including a duplicate automation-state object (automation_state alongside the declared automation_status) and the unfalsifiable `folders` block. All three invocations succeeded on the first attempt; no retries were needed and none of the response bodies were diffed against an error schema.
